newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan angry at Russian minister's Swiss trip.
newsitem.headline: Japan angry at Russian minister's Swiss trip.

text.p: Russia on Thursday found itself in a diplomatic spat with Japan over the last-minute cancellation of a visit to Tokyo by a senior Moscow official.

The row erupted over the travels of Russia's First Deputy Prime Minister Viktor Ilyushin who abruptly cancelled a planned visit to Tokyo in late February in favour of going to Lausanne in Switzerland as head of a Russian delegation to discuss the 2004 Olympics.
Ilyushin had telephoned Japan's Foreign Minister Yukihiko Ikeda two days before his scheduled arrival to say he had domestic matters to attend to.
"Frankly speaking, I cannot help but feel disappointed," Foreign Ministry spokesman Hiroshi Hashimoto told a news conference.
"Our government believes we deserve a satisfactory explanation from the Russian government," Hashimoto said.
Japan summoned Russian ambassador to Japan, Alexandre Panov, to the ministry on Wednesday to seek an explanation, officials said.
"But to this date, we have not received a satisfactory explanation," Hashimoto said.
Ilyushin's visit to Tokyo was to discuss trade and economic issues. The minister told Ikeda he hoped to reschedule the visit for some time between April and June.
Russian embassy officials were not immediately available for comment.
